column1: # tests/gates.tsv — THE declaration of every gate excise runs locally (LOCAL_GATES.md).
# One row per gate. The runners (scripts/test-tier.sh, scripts/run-full-suite.sh,
# scripts/release-smoke.sh) hold NO step list of their own: each derives its plan
# from this file through runner_manifest_plan <tier> in scripts/lib-runner.sh,
# which also validates it and refuses to run a defective manifest. A future
# GitHub Action consumes this same file; nothing is built for Actions here.
# Columns (13, tab-separated; '-' is the mandatory empty-cell placeholder):
#   name          slug; equals the ledger row name. Chunk rows <name>.chunkNN are derived.
#   class         BLOCK    fails on any failure — a NEW bug blocks a build
#                 IMPROVE  fails only on regression vs its ratchet file — keep working on it
#                 GRADE    never fails the run — a number vs the reference tools
#                 SELFTEST proves a gate can fail (falsifiability, #1012)
#                 SETUP    prepares the run; judges nothing. Still blocks on a
#                          real failure, but is not counted as a check (#1767)
#   tiers         comma set of t0,t1,full,t2. CHAIN: t0 ⊂ t1 ⊂ full (a t0 row runs in
#                 t1 and full too); t2 (release-smoke, Release config) only when listed.
#                 File order is execution order within every tier.
#   kind          script | test | project | project-chunked | fn
#   filter        dotnet test --filter for kind=test; '-' otherwise
#   ratchet       the checked-in floor an IMPROVE row compares against (must exist)
#   knownIssue    '-', '#N' (a FAIL is KNOWN while N is OPEN), or '#N/Substring'
#                 (KNOWN only when every failing test / the log matches Substring).
#                 A CLOSED N makes the report fail STALE. Never accept a red without one.
#   prereq        space-separated tool:NAME corpus:NAME env:NAME file:GLOB opt:NAME, or '-'
#   prereqPolicy  fail | skip — what a missing prerequisite (column or exit 77) becomes
#   checkpoint    ok | never — may --resume skip this row. Redaction rows are never.
#   oracle        independent | spec | self | none | na (who vouches for the verdict)
#   note          why this class and tier; measured cost with its date. Mandatory.
# scripts/test-tier.sh --list <tier> prints a tier's rows. Do not hand-copy them into docs.

Clean here = 871/877/881/913 s (logs/full-suite_Debug_20260915_213048, _222810, _20260916_000404, _002001), then ADD CONTENTION HEADROOM -> 2400s. ⚠️ THE CONTENTION FACTOR IS THE USEFUL ARTEFACT: measured +48% on this machine (1355 s in a git worktree alongside ~2.6 GB of idle MSBuild daemons, vs a clean worst of 913 s) -- not the ~30% that was guessed. Size a new row as 2x worst-clean PLUS that headroom. Why generous and not tight: this bound exists to end an UNBOUNDED stall (the recorded #1283 failure ran NINE HOURS), not to police quiet-vs-loaded variance. A false fire costs a whole run and teaches people to disregard BOUND EXCEEDED, which is the only way this gate can actually fail; 600 s of extra headroom costs nothing against a hang that would otherwise run all night, and 2400 s still bounds the worst case to well under an hour -- the property that matters. At 1800 s this row ran 1355 s = 75% of budget, uncomfortably close; 2400 s puts it at 56%. 2026-09-16 was the FIRST time this path ran at all, so one completion is one data point, not verification under load.
